title: Little Nemo: The Dream Master
subtitle: A journey through sleep
summary: Little Nemo: The Dream Master is Capcom’s NES platform adventure based on the animated film and, behind it, Winsor McCay’s comic-strip dreamer. Nemo travels through colourful dream worlds on a journey to rescue the king of Slumberland from the Nightmare King. His own abilities are limited, but friendly creatures can provide other ways to move. body: Little Nemo: The Dream Master is Capcom’s NES platform adventure based on the animated film and, behind it, Winsor McCay’s comic-strip dreamer. Nemo travels through colourful dream worlds on a journey to rescue the king of Slumberland from the Nightmare King. His own abilities are limited, but friendly creatures can provide other ways to move. The stages give those borrowed abilities a purpose: finding the keys needed to open an exit often requires exploring above, below and beyond the most obvious route through a scene.

Feeding candy to particular animals lets Nemo ride them or use their powers. A frog, gorilla or mole changes which parts of a level can be reached and how obstacles can be approached. Choosing a creature therefore amounts to choosing a method of exploration. The same wall or gap may become manageable with the appropriate helper. These changes give the dream setting a practical logic: strange encounters offer new movements, and the player learns to connect the appearance of an animal with a possible route.

The exit’s locks make collecting keys essential, but the required total becomes clear only when Nemo reaches the door. A stage can therefore demand a return to places passed earlier, using an animal’s ability to investigate more thoroughly. The levels extend in several directions rather than simply presenting a straight run to the right. That structure supports the dreamlike variety of their scenery while keeping a concrete objective in view. Each new landscape asks the player to learn how its creatures and passages fit together.
